Definition: from G4078; a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation):--snare.
BiblicalUsage: Pagis is the snare, the trap with a noose. That day shall come as a snare on all who dwell on the face of the earth, David prays that Israel's table become a snare, riches plunge men into a snare, and the devil's snare holds men captive until they recover themselves.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the snare warns me twice. The last day will trap the careless, and the love of money traps them sooner, but the snare can be broken and the captive set free.
